summary: Master reservoir engineering fundamentals. Learn PVT analysis, material balance, and SPE-PRMS reserve estimation to optimize asset recovery. Enroll today.
lede: Reservoir engineering examines how rock and fluid properties shape flow and production from subsurface reservoirs. For junior reservoir engineers, production technologists, petrophysicists and development geologists, the course supports production monitoring, forecasting and development planning. Learners assess rock and fluid properties, interpret PVT reports, identify drive mechanisms, and use material balance, pressure-transient and decline-curve analysis to estimate reservoir volumes and forecast production.
audienceIntro: This program is essential for technical professionals who require a robust understanding of how fluids move through porous media and how to manage those resources over the life of an asset.
modules: Fluid Phase Behavior and PVT Analysis
Reservoir Drive Mechanisms and Material Balance
Well Testing and Pressure Transient Analysis
Production Forecasting and Decline Curve Analysis
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of petroleum geology and undergraduate-level mathematics (algebra and basic calculus). No prior experience with simulation software is required, but a laptop with Microsoft Excel is necessary for the calculation exercises.
